title: Logic Apps vs Functions vs Power Automate
description: Choose between the three main Azure automation options based on who builds the workflow, what it connects to, and how it is governed.

data.text: Logic Apps vs Functions vs Power Automate

All three can react to an event and call other services, so the decision is rarely about capability. It is about who builds the automation, what it connects to, how much code it contains, and how it is governed and billed. Logic Apps is the Azure integration service, Functions is the code-first compute service, and Power Automate is the business-user automation service.

rows: Custom logic, transforms, and high-volume work
Medium; some custom code via inline actions
Full control in the runtime you choose
Low; limited to connectors and expressions

data.caption: Decide by asking who owns the automation and whether custom code is the core of the work.

data.title: Interview angle: they compose, they do not compete
data.text: A strong answer describes composition. A Logic App can receive an HTTP request, validate it, and call a Function to run a custom transformation, then publish the result to Service Bus. Power Automate can trigger the same Logic App from a SharePoint list. The choice is about the right layer: code where code belongs, orchestration where orchestration belongs, and citizen automation where that is safe and governed.
The Same Workflow in Each Tool

A workflow that reacts to an event and writes a result can be expressed in all three. Seeing the shape of each makes the trade-off concrete: a Logic App is a declarative connector graph, a Function is code you deploy, and a Power Automate flow is a designer-built flow owned by a business team.

data.title: Logic Apps workflow definition (trigger plus action)
data.content: The trigger and the action are declared; the connector does the work. There is no application code to build or deploy.

data.title: The same trigger as an Azure Function (code you own)
data.content: The logic is code: a trigger binding and the extraction in C#. This is the tool to reach for when the core of the work is custom.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Logic Apps is for orchestration and connectors; Functions is for custom code.
Power Automate targets business users inside Microsoft 365 and Dataverse.
Choose Logic Apps when the workflow is mostly connecting systems and handling approvals.
Choose Functions when the workload is code-heavy, high-volume, or needs precise control.
The three compose: a Logic App can call a Function, and Power Automate can trigger a Logic App.
Governance differs: Azure resource controls for Logic Apps and Functions, environment policies for Power Automate.
